scenario:
A wholesale distribution company specializing in industrial tapes is developing an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system to manage its inventory, pricing, and order fulfillment processes. The company deals with various sizes of tape products, each having different pricing structures based on order quantities. To optimize operations, the ERP system should manage detailed information about each product, including item size, item number, packaging details (items per case), and pricing tiers for different order quantities.

The system needs to handle complex pricing rules, applying discounts based on the volume of items ordered. It should also track inventory levels, lead times, and shipping delays, facilitating efficient order management and customer satisfaction. Additionally, the ERP should support analytics to predict demand, adjust pricing strategies, and manage supplier relationships effectively.

The system will integrate with the company's existing sales and customer management tools, providing a comprehensive view of the business operations. It should offer detailed reporting capabilities for inventory turnover, cost analysis, and sales performance. The ERP will also manage customer orders, ensuring that pricing is correctly applied according to the specified discount tiers.
